mercy_translation.text:
After what has been said, it is fitting for you to learn this also and to place it as a beginning for the things not yet spoken: marvel greatly that since the Savior's coming, idolatry has no longer increased, but what existed is diminishing and little by little ceasing; Greek wisdom no longer advances, and what existed is now fading; demons no longer deceive by apparitions, oracles, and magical practices, but whenever they dare and attempt such things they are put to shame by the sign of the cross.

To put it briefly, observe how the Savior's teaching increases everywhere, while all idolatry and everything opposed to the faith of Christ decreases daily, grows weak, and falls. Seeing this, worship the Savior who is over all, the mighty Word of God, and condemn those things that are diminishing and disappearing before him.

For just as when the sun is present darkness no longer has strength, and whatever remains anywhere is driven away, so when the divine manifestation of God the Word came, the darkness of idols no longer had power, and all regions of the inhabited world were illumined by his teaching.

It is like a king who reigns but is not visible in a certain region because he remains inside his own house. Often disorderly people, taking advantage of his absence, proclaim themselves rulers. Each puts on the appearance of a king and deceives the innocent, and people are misled by the title because they hear that there is a king but do not see him—especially because they cannot enter the royal house. But when the true king comes out and appears, then the fraudulent pretenders are exposed by his presence, and the people, seeing the true king, abandon those who formerly deceived them.

So in earlier times demons and human beings deceived others by assigning divine honor to themselves. But when the Word of God appeared in a body and made his own Father known to us, then the deception of demons disappeared and ceased; and human beings, looking to the true divine Word of the Father, abandoned idols and thereafter came to know the true God.

This is a sign that Christ is God the Word and the Power of God. For human things pass away while the word of Christ remains. Therefore it is clear to all that the things which pass away are temporary, while the One who remains is God and the true Son of God, the only-begotten Word.

translator_notes: Translated directly from the Greek source.
The true-king analogy concludes Athanasius' contrast between Christ's enduring rule and rival cults he considered deceptive.
Statements about the decline of ancient religions are Athanasius' fourth-century apologetic claims and should be read historically.
